title: Science under Threat? A Natural Experiment in Economics
abstract: arXiv:2608.14164v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Academic freedom has come under growing strain worldwide. To study whether and how academics respond to political pressure, we exploit a natural experiment: the publication in early 2025 of a "blacklist" of words flagged by the U.S. government. We find that the release of this list led to a sharp reduction in the use of these flagged words among economists at universities that rely heavily on federal funding, relative to scholars from institutions that are less dependent on federal funding or based in the UK. The drop is driven by content related to gender, race, and environment. We show that changes are not simply semantic but reflect actual paper content and that neither the individual funding status nor time-invariant author characteristics are driving the effects. translated_title: 科学面临威胁？经济学中的一项自然实验
translated_abstract: 学术自由在全球范围内正面临日益增长的压力。为了研究学者是否以及如何应对政治压力，我们利用了一项自然实验：2025年初美国政府发布的一份“黑名单”词汇表。我们发现，这份名单的发布导致高度依赖联邦资金的大学中的经济学家使用这些标记词汇的频率显著减少，相比之下，那些对联邦资金依赖较少的机构或位于英国的学者变化较小。这种下降主要集中在与性别、种族和环境相关的内容上。我们表明，这些变化不仅仅是语义上的，而是反映了论文的实际内容，并且个人资助状态或作者的不变特征并非驱动因素。我们还记录了按院系质量和作者性别、种族划分的有趣异质性效应。我们的发现与学者对政治压力作出回应的观点一致。
tldr: 本文通过自然实验发现，美国政府的词汇黑名单导致依赖联邦资金的经济学家在论文中减少使用敏感词汇，尤其是性别、种族和环境相关术语，表明学者会因政治压力调整研究内容。
en_tdlr: This paper uses a natural experiment to show that a U.S. government word blacklist led economists at federally funded universities to reduce usage of flagged terms, especially related to gender, race, and environment, indicating scholars adjust research in response to political pressure.
